df1<-read.csv("C:/xxx/yyy.csv",header=TRUE,quote="\"")

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: Can I read files locally over 60MB? not uploading.
parts:
When you say the limit on uploads is 30MB, are you referring to the limits for shinyapps.io?  

If you are working with shinyapps.io, you will want the file that you are loading to be in the same directory (or a sub-directory) of the application.  Absolute paths are a problem because when you transfer an application up to shinyapps.io, it will only know about the directory that the application is in, and the sub-directories so any files that are references relative to your machine are not going to be in the same location on shinyapps.io.

messages.subject: Re: Can I read files locally over 60MB? not uploading.
parts:
You can change the upload limit using

options(shiny.maxRequestSize = 9*1024^2)  # Set the limit to 9MB

or use the value -1 for no limit at all.

For reading, there is no limit except for memory. What kind of failure are you seeing?
